about.description:
LUE is software supporting the representation and numerical simulation of geographical
systems. Using LUE, model developers can develop models using a syntax that looks very
similar to map algebra, in either Python or C++. Given such a model, modellers can simulate
real-world geographical systems with a large extent and at high resolutions. LUE models
can be executed on small laptops and on large cluster partitions.

LUE is the result of multiple research projects performed by the Computational Geography
group at Utrecht University in the Netherlands. One of the focus areas of this group is
to improve on the concepts and design of numerical simulation frameworks for geographical
systems, with respect to their functionality and performance.

LUE supports both agent-based and field-based modelling of geographical systems, with the
support for field-based modelling currently being the most mature.
about.summary: LUE scientific database and environmental modelling framework.

raw_meta_yaml:
schema_version: 1

context:
  version: "0.3.11"

package:
  name: lue
  version: ${{ version }}

source:
  # NOTE: Use these once new version of LUE is actually released
  # NOTE: Use these while preparing for a LUE release
  # git_url: https://github.com/computationalgeography/lue.git
  # git_depth: 1
  url: https://lue.computationalgeography.org/download/lue-${{ version }}.tar.bz2
  sha256: 6cc8b255543b979c877d265435ed1134d74dd124038c471c3c742c4955054ab1

build:
  number: 1
  skip: osx and x86_64

requirements:
  build:
    # Packages needed on the build platform, for building LUE
    - ${{ compiler("c") }}
    - ${{ compiler("cxx") }}
    - ${{ stdlib("c") }}
    - cmake
    - ninja
    - if: build_platform != target_platform
      then: cross-python_${{ target_platform }}
    - if: build_platform != target_platform
      then: python
    - if: build_platform != target_platform
      then: numpy
  host:
    # Packages needed on the build platform, containing stuff specific to the target platform
    # Any run_exports get implicitly exported to the run section
    # - shared libraries, interpreters
    - cxxopts
    - docopt-ng  # templatize.py
    - hdf5
    - hpx <2.0.0
    - jinja2  # templatize.py
    - libgdal
    - nlohmann_json
    - numpy
    - pybind11
    - python
  run:
    # Packages needed on the runtime platform, for using LUE
    # Only list packages whose meta.yaml doesn't contain a run_exports already
    # - build-time: headers, libraries
    # - runtime: shared libraries, interpreter
    - docopt-ng  # lue.qa
    - matplotlib-base  # lue.qa
    - python
    - python-dateutil  # lue.qa

tests:
  - python:
      imports:
        - lue
        - lue.data_model
        - lue.framework
        - lue.framework_x
        - lue.pcraster
        - lue.qa.scalability
      pip_check: false
  - script:
      - lue_translate -h
      - lue_validate -h
      - if: not win
        then: lue_calculate.py -h
      - if: not win
        then: lue_scalability.py -h
